causal.assumptions_right: The cash-versus-strip gap was real; CAD policy was easier than the 2027 contract.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: Ownership and holding period. Other desks already received CAD. A sub-day hold cannot harvest a multi-quarter easing gap, and the bid was crowded before entry.
causal.causal_divergence: Zero result was not a one-day falsification of CAD easing versus 3.40. Price did not pay the late receiver because the receive was already owned.
causal.future_implication: Do not receive CORRA Mar27 while other desks are crowded received. Cash 2.30 versus 3.125 is not permission to join.
causal.observed_reality: Flat scratch in under a day: entry 3.40, exit 3.40. The freeze now shows Mar27 at 3.125 versus CORRA cash 2.30 with the receive crowded on other desks.
causal.original_belief: Long/receive CORRA Mar27 at 3.40 was a cheap policy-path receive versus easier CAD cash, with room for the 2027 strip to rally.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With crowding known, the receive would not have been opened for a same-session hold; the book would have stayed flat.

items.expression_assessment: Outright CORRA Mar27 receive was the consensus expression; better ownership was elsewhere or flat.
items.future_rule: No new receive on CORRA 2027-03 while crowding is flagged, regardless of cash-strip cheapness; if the hold cannot extend beyond one session, do not enter.
items.lesson: Cheap versus cash is not an entry when the receive is already the crowded desk position.
items.timing_assessment: Sub-day scratch was an entry into an already-owned bid, not a timed harvest.
items.what_failed: Opened a crowded CAD receive with no ownership edge and no holding period long enough to monetize the cash-strip gap.

causal.assumptions_right: Paying the less-crowded AUD path had ownership edge relative to CAD receive; a short window was enough to clip 2bp.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: A 2bp two-session gain is not proof the RBA hike cycle was harvested as a structural thesis; path and tenor beyond Mar27 were not required for the result.
causal.causal_divergence: Result matched the anti-crowd pay, then stopped. It did not demonstrate that scaling AUD pays, or recycling CAD, was licensed.
causal.future_implication: Keep preferring unowned AUD pay over crowded CAD receive when expansion is allowed; do not read a 2bp clip as a green light to reopen either leg.
causal.observed_reality: Brief pay worked: entry 4.86, exit 4.88 over two sessions. The freeze now shows AONIA cash 4.35 versus Jun27 5.005.
causal.original_belief: Short/pay AONIA Mar27 at 4.86 was the less-owned hike-path expression versus a crowded CAD receive.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: The pay would still have been the correct side versus crowded CORRA receive; it would not have been treated as confirmation to re-enter CAD or to enlarge AONIA.

items.no_new_lesson: Bounded ordinary variance around a sound anti-crowd pay; process remains sound. Do not overfit a two-session 2bp win into a new rule beyond keep fading crowded CAD receive.
items.sizing_assessment: Size produced a small 2bp clip without turning a brief timing window into a concentrated structural bet.
items.thesis_assessment: Anti-crowd pay versus crowded CAD receive was the right ownership lens; the clip was too small to call the structural hike path complete.
items.what_worked: Paid a less-owned AONIA Mar27 expression and exited after a small, timely 2bp move rather than joining CAD receive.

causal.assumptions_right: CAD outperformed the dollar over the holding window. Closing the FX short and expressing the residual view in the March 2027 pay moved risk toward the rates path.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: Uniqueness of ownership. The pitch treated a CAD-bull spot short as a distinct crowded-dollar fade rather than a duplicate overlay on dove/carry receives and leftover dollar-king CAD.
causal.causal_divergence: The gap is ownership uniqueness, not whether CAD-bull was confirmed. Short USDCAD did not uniquely fade crowded long-dollar; it stacked the same CAD-bull the desk already owned. The later March 2027 pay is the tell that the distinct expression was the rates path and spot was the second overlay.
causal.future_implication: Do not re-short USDCAD as a crowded-dollar fade while dove/carry CAD-bull remains on. Hold the existing March 2027 pay. Do not add a March 2027 receive as a balance to the closed FX short.
causal.observed_reality: USDCAD fell from 1.42 to 1.41 over about 19 days and was closed on 21 October, after which the desk paid CORRA March 2027. Direction paid. Ownership was not unique: carry and dove receives plus leftover dollar-king long already supplied CAD-bull.
causal.original_belief: Short USDCAD was a unique fade of a crowded long-dollar book, cleaner than adding another dollar short, and distinct from rates CAD-bull already owned.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: On the same information — crowded long-dollar narrative plus CAD-bull already owned in dove/carry receives and dollar-king leftover — a uniqueness check would have rejected short USDCAD and kept risk in a CORRA pay or in flat FX.

items.expression_assessment: Failed. Spot FX was not the unique instrument. The unique remaining expression was the March 2027 pay; USDCAD was the crowded overlay.

facts.invalidation: The fade is wrong if USDCAD holds bid or squeezes higher while the desk remains or adds long, implying the long is not a crowded supply source.

items.future_rule: Before adding spot FX as a crowded-dollar fade or CAD-bull, list existing rates and leftover FX ownership. If the new trade is the same CAD-bull overlay, skip spot and hold the existing rates pay. Do not mint a March 2027 CORRA receive to balance a closed FX short.
items.lesson: A profitable CAD-bull spot fade is still a bad expression if the desk already owns the same CAD-bull through dove and carry receives and leftover dollar-king positioning. Uniqueness of ownership is the trade, not a restatement of the CAD tape.
items.sizing_assessment: Sizing is not the defect. The error was stacking a second CAD-bull expression rather than the dollars put on the short.
items.thesis_assessment: CAD-bull versus the dollar was fine as a macro lean. The claim that spot was a unique fade of crowded long-dollar was not.
items.timing_assessment: The roughly 19-day window captured the 1.42 to 1.41 move and the 21 October close. Timing of the FX trade is not the defect.
items.what_failed: The ownership-uniqueness screen. Short USDCAD was sold as a crowded-dollar fade when it was another CAD-bull overlay on dove/carry receives and leftover dollar-king long.
items.what_worked: Direction paid: USDCAD fell from 1.42 to 1.41 over about 19 days, and the post-close rotation into a March 2027 CORRA pay moved residual risk toward the rates path.

causal.assumptions_right: Another receive would have joined the crowd that was already owned. Cutting once the pay itself was the hike story matched the ownership rule.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: The cash gap was treated as if it proved the receive was wrong, while that receive kept being the winning flow. The short was then held into the window when the pay had become the crowded hike.
causal.causal_divergence: The crowded receive did not exhaust. It compressed, the fade lost money, and by the cover the position was the same hike expression the tape was already discussing.
causal.future_implication: Do not pay the next front contract because it looks rich to cash, and do not receive SOFR now only because headlines call the hike crowded while bond futures are still falling.
causal.observed_reality: The implied yield fell from the entry, reductions locked in the loss, and the residual was covered once that pay sat with the public hike story.
causal.original_belief: Paying March 2027 Canada bills would fade a receive that was already the owned front-end idea, and the gap versus cash was treated as proof that receive was crowded.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With the same entry information the pay should have been skipped. A cash gap plus an existing receive is not an ownership extreme.

facts.invalidation: The pay is wrong if CRAH27 implied keeps compressing toward CORRA cash 2.26 while the existing receive stays on, or if Canada inflation/oil pressure reverses with labor still cool.

items.future_rule: Skip a new front-end pay or receive when the only crowding evidence is the gap to cash, unless a listed instrument shows the other side is the owned position and the working flow has stalled.
items.lesson: A front-end pay is not an unowned fade just because the contract looks rich to cash. Once that pay is the public hike story, it is the crowded side.
items.thesis_assessment: The ownership objection was right at entry. The pay stopped being that fade once it became the hike consensus.
items.what_failed: The March 2027 Canada pay was opened as a fade of a receive that looked rich to cash. The implied yield then fell, reductions locked in the loss, and the residual was covered only after that pay sat with the public hike story.

causal.assumptions_right: The cross extreme was the owned side, the short paid, and covering once the move was visible avoided turning a completed fade into the new consensus short.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: A separate Canada pay was still on beside the cross. The cross fade did not need its full planned horizon once the move was the visible trade.
causal.causal_divergence: There was no material divergence. The extreme was faded, the cross mean-reverted, and the cover happened because the trade had become visible.
causal.future_implication: Keep fading a cross only while it is the less-owned extreme, and cover it once the move is the visible trade.
causal.observed_reality: The cross fell from the entry area and was covered once the move was already the visible trade.
causal.original_belief: Australia-kiwi near 1.25 was the crowded long-cross extreme, a cleaner ownership fade than dollar-yen near its highs.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With the same entry information the cross short was the right expression versus adding dollar-yen or another Canada receive.

facts.invalidation: The cross fade is invalidated if Australian-kiwi holds 1.2453 and extends while kiwi-dollar stays pinned at 0.5622. The residual Canada short is invalidated if March implied yield keeps falling toward cash at 2.52.

items.no_new_lesson: The original process remains sound. The gain was the intended fade of an extended cross, realized inside the risk budget, and it does not change the rule that a cash-gap receive is not an entry.
items.thesis_assessment: The extreme-cross fade was the right ownership trade and was closed when the move had become the visible trade.
items.what_worked: Shorting the extended Australia-kiwi cross and covering once that move was the visible trade captured the ownership asymmetry without joining a new crowded short.
